question.prompt:
Given triangle \(PQR\) with \(\overline{RS}\) bisecting \(\angle R,\) \(\overline{PQ}\) extended to \(D,\) and \(\angle n\) a right angle, then:

[Figure 1](figures/1954_AMC_12_Q37_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The right angle lets us connect \(m\) to half the angle at \(R\).

[Figure 1](figures/1954_AMC_12_Q37_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(p,q,m\) denote the measures of the marked angles, and let \(r=\angle PRQ\). Let \(U\) and \(V\) be the intersections of the sloping line through \(D\) with \(PR\) and \(RS\), respectively. Since the marked angle \(n\) is a right angle, this sloping line is perpendicular to \(RS\). Thus triangle \(RUV\) is right at \(V\).

Because \(RS\) bisects the angle at \(R\), we have \(\angle URV=r/2\). The two acute angles of triangle \(RUV\) are complementary, so
\[
m=90^\circ-\frac r2.
\]
Meanwhile, the angle sum in triangle \(PQR\) gives \(p+q=180^\circ-r\). Therefore
\[
m=\frac{180^\circ-r}{2}=\frac{p+q}{2}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Use the bisected angle at R
